Rashi on Pesachim 6a:10:1.english: Which is not found in your possession - For that corner is handed over to the non-Jew.

Rashi on Pesachim 6a:11:1.hebrew: כופה עליו את הכלי - דהא לא חזי לטלטולי ואפוקי. ומיהו, בבל יראה לא עבר, דהא בטליה בליביה מאתמול, כדאמרינן לקמן: "הבודק צריך שיבטל בלבו"; אלא משום שלא ישכח ויאכלנו — צריך כפיית כלי:
Rashi on Pesachim 6a:11:1.english: Covers it with a vessel - For it is not fit to be handled and taken out. However, he does not violate [the prohibition of] "it shall not be seen," for he already nullified it in his heart yesterday, as we say below: "One who searches must nullify [it] in his heart." Rather, lest he forget and eat it, covering [it with] a vessel is required.

Rashi on Pesachim 6a:11:2.english: People distance themselves from it - Even on weekdays, he is accustomed to separate from it.

Rashi on Pesachim 6a:12:1.hebrew: חמצו של נכרי - המופקד אצלו ולא קיבל עליו אחריות, דמותר לשהותו:
Rashi on Pesachim 6a:12:1.english: Leaven belonging to a gentile - Which is deposited with him and he did not accept [financial] responsibility for it, so that it is permitted to retain it:

Rashi on Pesachim 6a:12:2.hebrew: עושה לו מחיצה - בארבעה עשר, משום היכר, שלא ישכח ויאכלנו. ולא סגי ליה בכפיית כלי כל שבעה, שהכלי ניטל לצורך. ומיהו, ההוא דלעיל לא אפשר ליה במחיצה, ומשום חד יומא סגי ליה בכפיית כלי, ובלילה יבערנו:
Rashi on Pesachim 6a:12:2.english: He erects a barrier for it - On the fourteenth [of Nisan], as a conspicuous marker, so that he will not forget and eat it. And it is not sufficient for him to overturn a vessel [over it] for all seven [days], for the vessel is [liable to be] taken for [some] need. However, that [case] above — it was not possible for him [to erect] a barrier, and for one day, overturning a vessel is sufficient for him, and at night he will burn it.

Rashi on Pesachim 6a:13:1.english: One who sets sail - From dry land to the sea.

Rashi on Pesachim 6a:13:2.english: In a caravan - To a distant place.

Rashi on Pesachim 6a:13:3.hebrew: קודם שלשים יום - לפסח. ולקמן מפרש: כנגד ששואלין בהלכות הפסח קודם הפסח שלשים יום, ומאז חל עליו להיזהר בצרכי הפסח:
Rashi on Pesachim 6a:13:3.english: Before thirty days - Prior to Passover. And later, [the Gemara] explains: Corresponding to [the rule] that one inquires into the laws of Passover thirty days before Passover, and from that time on it becomes incumbent upon him to be careful regarding the requirements of Passover.

Rashi on Pesachim 6a:13:4.english: His intention is to return - During the days of Passover:

Rashi on Pesachim 6a:14:1.hebrew: אפילו מראש השנה נמי - דכי הדר ביה בימי הפסח, עבר עליה. וההיא שעתא לאו ברשותיה היא דליבטליה — שהרי איסור הנאה הוא ואינו שלו — וכשראהו, עובר עליה:
Rashi on Pesachim 6a:14:1.english: Even from Rosh HaShana as well - For when he returns [home] during the days of Passover, he will violate [the prohibition]; and at that time, it is not in his domain to nullify it — for it is forbidden for benefit and is not his — and when he sees it, he violates [the prohibition].

Rashi on Pesachim 6a:15:1.hebrew: אוצר - שהכניס שם תבואה, ותחתיה חמץ. ואמרינן לקמן: חמץ שנפלה עליו מפולת, הרי הוא כמבוער:
Rashi on Pesachim 6a:15:1.english: A storehouse - That he brought grain in there, and beneath it was leaven. And we say below: Leaven upon which a collapse fell is regarded as eliminated:

Rashi on Pesachim 6a:15:2.english: Within thirty [days], he must remove [it] - For ab initio, this is not its [proper] removal.

Rashi on Pesachim 6a:15:3.hebrew: קודם שלשים - לא חלה חובת ביעור עליו, וכי מטי ההיא שעתא, לא מחוייב, כדאמרן — דהא נפלה עליו מפולת:
Rashi on Pesachim 6a:15:3.english: Before thirty [days] - The obligation of removal had not taken effect upon him; and when that time arrives, he is not obligated [to remove it], as we said — since a collapse has fallen upon it.

Rashi on Pesachim 6a:1:1.hebrew: להכי איצטריך לא ימצא - משום דבעלמא לאו כממון דמי, איצטריך קרא למימר דגבי חמץ מיהא מתסר:
Rashi on Pesachim 6a:1:1.english: For this [reason], “it shall not be found” was necessary - Because in general [an object that causes monetary loss] is not considered like money, the verse was necessary to state that regarding leaven at least, it is prohibited.

Rashi on Pesachim 6a:1:2.hebrew: הואיל וכי איתיה הדר - הוא גופיה למריה בעיניה, וזה עדיין לא נאבד. וכי אמרה ר' שמעון לההוא — היכא דאינו בעין, כגון גבי גונב קדשים שהיו הבעלים חייבין באחריותן, אמר רבי שמעון: אף על פי שאין כפל להקדש, דכתיב "לרעהו" ולא להקדש, הכא חייב, דכיון דזה חייב באחריותן "רעהו" קרינא ביה, דהא גרם לו להתחייב ממון:
Rashi on Pesachim 6a:1:2.english: Since when it is [intact], it returns - It itself [returns] to its owner intact, and this [leaven] has not yet been lost. And when Rabbi Shimon stated that [principle — that an item causing monetary liability is treated like money — it was] where it is not intact, such as in the case of one who steals consecrated property for which the owner was financially responsible, [where] Rabbi Shimon said: Even though there is no double payment for consecrated property, as it is written: “To his neighbor” (Exodus 22:8) and not to consecrated property, here he is liable, because since this [owner] is financially responsible for it, we apply [the term] “his neighbor” to it, for he [the thief] caused him to incur monetary liability.

Rashi on Pesachim 6a:2:1.english: Arnona - The king takes a tenth of the animals and of the grain.

Rashi on Pesachim 6a:2:2.hebrew: חייבת בבכורה - דקיימא לן: כל שיד נכרי באמצע — פטורה מן הבכורה, שנאמר (במדבר ג׳:י״ג) ״לי כל בכור בישראל״ — אבל לא באחרים. ועדר זה, שעישורו של מלך בתוכו — חייבת בבכורה לתת לכהן הבכורות שלהם, או לא:
Rashi on Pesachim 6a:2:2.english: [Is it] obligated in [the law of] the firstborn - For we maintain: Any [animal] in which the hand of a gentile is involved is exempt from [the law of] the firstborn, as it is stated (Numbers 3:13): "Mine is every firstborn in Israel" — but not among others. And [as for] this herd, in which the king's tenth is within it — is it obligated in [the law of] the firstborn, to give to the priest their firstborns, or not?

Rashi on Pesachim 6a:2:3.english: Where he can dismiss him - [Namely,] the gentile, with money.

Rashi on Pesachim 6a:2:4.hebrew: לא תיבעי לן - כיון דאכתי לא זכה נכרי בהן, ודינו אינו קבוע בהן יותר ממעות, איכא למימר: לא יתן לו בהמות אלא מעות:
Rashi on Pesachim 6a:2:4.english: We do not raise the dilemma - Since the gentile has not yet acquired [a share in] them, and his legal claim is not fixed upon them any more than upon money, it can be said: He will not give him animals, but rather money.

Rashi on Pesachim 6a:4:1.hebrew: ואע"ג דמצי מסלק ליה - דכל כמה דלא סלקיה, ידו שייכא בבהמות:
Rashi on Pesachim 6a:4:1.english: Even though he can dismiss him - For as long as he has not dismissed him, his [the gentile's] hand is associated with the animals.

Rashi on Pesachim 6a:4:2.hebrew: עיסת ארנונא חייבת - ואע"ג דעיסת נכרי פטורה, ואוכל ישראל בלא חלה, דהא עריסותיכם כתיב — זו חייבת, דלית לה קלא, והרואה אומר: שלו היא, ואוכלה בלא חלה. אבל בבהמה אית לה קלא. והדתניא חייבת — בעיסה הוא דתניא:
Rashi on Pesachim 6a:4:2.english: Dough of the royal tax is obligated - And even though a gentile's dough is exempt, and an Israelite may eat [it] without [separating] ḥalla, for behold, "your kneading bowls" is written — this [dough] is obligated, as it does not generate publicity, and an observer will say: "It is his, and he eats it without [separating] ḥalla." But regarding an animal, it generates publicity. And that which was taught [in the baraita], "It is obligated" — it was taught regarding dough.

Rashi on Pesachim 6a:6:1.hebrew: יחד לו בית - כלומר, לא קיבלו עליו, אלא אמר ליה: ״הרי הבית לפניך, הנח באחת מן הזויות״ — אין זקוק לבער:
Rashi on Pesachim 6a:6:1.english: He designated a house for him - That is to say, he did not accept [responsibility for] it upon himself, but rather said to him: “Behold, the house is before you; place [it] in one of the corners” — he is not required to remove [it].

Rashi on Pesachim 6a:6:2.hebrew: אין זקוק לבער - לא הזקיקוהו להוציא את הנכרי מן הבית, כדאמרן: ״אבל אתה רואה של אחרים״:
Rashi on Pesachim 6a:6:2.english: [He] is not required to remove [it] - They did not obligate him to remove the gentile from the house, as we said: “But you may see that of others.”

Rashi on Pesachim 6a:7:1.english: What is he saying - How does he derive [this] from “It shall not be found”?

Rashi on Pesachim 6a:7:2.hebrew: הפקידו אצלו - וקביל עליה אחריות, כדמפרש ואזיל — זקוק לבער:
Rashi on Pesachim 6a:7:2.english: [If] he deposited it with him - And he accepted [financial] responsibility for it, as [the Gemara] goes on to explain — [he is] required to remove [it].

Rashi on Pesachim 6a:8:1.hebrew: לעולם אסיפא - ולא ימצא משמע: המצוי בידך לכל חפצך — היינו דקביל עליה אחריות, דהוי כדידיה:
Rashi on Pesachim 6a:8:1.english: Actually, [it refers] to the last clause - And "it shall not be found" implies: [that which is] found in your possession for all your needs — that is, where he accepted responsibility for it, so that it is [considered] like his own.

Rashi on Pesachim 6a:9:1.hebrew: אף במקום שאמרו להשכיר - בפ"ק דע"א תנן: אין משכירין בתים לנכרים בארץ ישראל, אבל בסוריא משכירין, וכל שכן בחוצה לארץ. ואף במקום שהתירו להשכיר — לא לבית דירה התיר, אלא להעמיד בו בהמות ועצים, ולא שידור הוא בה:
Rashi on Pesachim 6a:9:1.english: Even in a place where they said to rent - In the first chapter of [Tractate] Avodah Zarah we learned: One may not rent houses to gentiles in the Land of Israel, but in Syria one may rent [them], and all the more so outside of the Land [of Israel]. And even in a place where they permitted renting — [the Tanna] did not permit [it] for a residence, but [only] to keep animals and wood in it, and not that he should reside in it.

Tosafot on Pesachim 6a:11:1.hebrew: כופה עליו כלי - אע"ג דאיכא למ"ד בפ' כירה (שבת מג.): "אין כלי ניטל אלא לדבר הניטל" — איכא לאוקמי בצריך למקומו. אי נמי, הכא שרי משום דילמא אתי למיכליה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 6a:11:1.english: Covers it with a vessel - Even though there is an authority who holds in the chapter [entitled] Kira (Shabbat 43a) [that] a vessel may be handled only for the sake of an item that may be handled, [this ruling] can be established [as referring to a case where] he needs its place. Alternatively, here it is permitted lest he come to eat it.

Tosafot on Pesachim 6a:2:1.hebrew: התם דמצי מסלק ליה - הק' ר"י: דבפ' איזהו נשך (ב"מ דף ע: ושם) אמר, דהמקבל צאן ברזל מן הנכרי — הוולדות פטורים מן הבכורה, אף על גב דמצי מסלק ליה לנכרי בזוזי, כדאמר התם: כיון דאלו בעי נכרי זוזי ולא משכח, שקול בהמה. ותי' ר"י: דשאני התם, שמתחלה היתה הבהמה של נכרי; וכיון דאי בעי זוזי ולא משכח שקיל בהמה — לא נפקא מרשותיה. אבל כשהבהמה של ישראל, ומצי מסלק ליה לנכרי בזוזי — לא נכנסה לרשותו:
Tosafot on Pesachim 6a:2:1.english: "There, where he can dismiss him" - Ri asked: For in the chapter [entitled] Eizehu Neshech (Bava Metzia 70b, and there) [the Gemara] says that [in the case of] one who accepts tzon barzel [iron-flock animals] from a gentile, the offspring are exempt from [the obligation of] the firstborn, even though he can dismiss the gentile with money, as [the Gemara] says there: Since if the gentile wants money and does not find [any], he takes the animal. And Ri answered: It is different there, because initially the animal belonged to the gentile; and since if he wants money and does not find [any] he takes the animal, it never left his domain. But when the animal belongs to a Jew, and he can dismiss the gentile with money, it never entered his [the gentile's] domain.

Tosafot on Pesachim 6a:4:1.hebrew: בהמת ארנונא פטורה מן הבכורה אע"ג דמצי מסלק ליה - והא דתניא "חייבת" — פ"ה דגבי עיסה תניא. וק' לרשב"א, דהא גבי בהמה תניא בהדיא בתוספתא דחייבת בבכורה, וכן גבי עיסה תניא: "עיסת ארנונא חייבת בחלה, אע"ג דלא מצי מסלק ליה". ואית ספרים דגרסי: "בהמת ארנונא פטורה, והוא דלא מצי מסלק ליה"; ולפי זה מתיישבות שתי הברייתות:
Tosafot on Pesachim 6a:4:1.english: An animal of arnona is exempt from the firstborn, even though he can dismiss him - And that which is taught [in a baraita], "It is obligated" — the Kuntres [Rashi] explained that it was taught regarding dough. And the Rashba raises a difficulty: For regarding an animal, it is explicitly taught in the Tosefta that it is obligated in [the law of] the firstborn; and similarly regarding dough it is taught: "Dough of arnona is obligated in challah even though he cannot dismiss him." And there are books that read: "An animal of arnona is exempt, and that is [specifically] when he cannot dismiss him"; and according to this, both baraitot are reconciled.

Tosafot on Pesachim 6a:6:1.hebrew: יחד לו בית - פ"ה דלא קיבל עליו אחריות, אלא אמר ליה: "הרי הבית לפניך". וק' לר"י: מאי איריא יחד? אפילו לא יחד נמי! והכי נמי מסיק בסמוך: "למימר דשכירות קניא?!". ופר"ת דאפילו באחריות מיירי; ומשום הכי מפיק מ"לא ימצא" — דלא חשיב מצוי, כיון שיחד לו בית. ורב פפא אית ליה מסברא: כיון שיחד לו בית, הוי כאלו קיבל עליו אחריות על חמצו של נכרי בביתו של נכרי:
Tosafot on Pesachim 6a:6:1.english: "He designated a house for him" - Rashi explained that the Jew did not accept responsibility for the leaven, but rather said to him: "Here is the house before you." And the Ri questioned this: Why specifically if he designated a house? Even if he did not designate one, it should also be permitted! And so too the Gemara concludes nearby: "Is that to say that rental acquires?!". And Rabbeinu Tam explained that the baraita is dealing even where the Jew accepted responsibility; and for this reason the Gemara derives it from "it shall not be found" — that it is not considered "found" in your possession, since he designated a house for him. And Rav Pappa holds based on reasoning: Since he designated a house for him, it is as though he accepted responsibility for a gentile's leaven in a gentile's house.
